U1: Alternative DLQ configuration with exception headers
U2: OOTB module to consume database changes as event streams (CDC)
U3: Native support for RabbitMQ cluster HA/FT in Spring AMQP
U4: Upgrade Gemfire to 8.1, depends on Spring Data Gosling GA
U5: Deploy stream in same container with leader election and failover
U6: Upgrade to SI milestone/GA release for JMX improvements
U7: Upgrade to SI Kafka release
U8: Upgrade to Spring Boot 1.2.3 with various dependency updates

Let me think about this as a software developer responsible for implementing this increment.

First, let me note that these user stories reference "XD" (Spring XD), "SI" (Spring Integration), and "Spring AMQP" - so this is really about Spring XD (a predecessor to Spring Cloud Data Flow) rather than core Spring Framework. Spring XD was a project that handled stream/batch processing.

Let me create a WBS-based estimation:

For U1 (Alternative DLQ with exception headers):
- Design: How to add configuration option for alternative DLQ
- Implementation: Add DLQ configuration support with header propagation
- Testing: Unit and integration tests
- Documentation: Update docs

For U2 (DB change event streams - CDC):
- This is a large feature - Debezium-like functionality
- Design the CDC module
- Implementation of source module
- Integration with various sinks (Kafka, Hadoop, DB)
- Testing

For U3 (Native Rabbit cluster HA/FT support in Spring AMQP):
- Research Rabbit cluster setup
- Design connection management
- Implementation
- Testing failover scenarios

For U4 (Upgrade Gemfire 8.1):
- Dependency updates
- API compatibility checks
- Testing
- Spring Data Gosling sync

For U5 (Colocated stream deployment + leader election):
- Design container architecture changes
- Implement leader election
- Implement failover logic
- Testing

For U6 (SI upgrade):
- Dependency upgrade
- Test for JMX changes
- Fix any breakage

For U7 (SI Kafka upgrade):
- Dependency upgrade
- Test and fix

For U8 (Spring Boot 1.2.3 + dependency sync):
- POM updates for all listed dependencies
- Resolve conflicts
- Test suite fixes

Plus common activities:
- Project setup, planning
- Integration testing across all changes
- Documentation updates
- Release management

technical_and_design_decisions: The increment targets Spring XD (and adjacent Spring projects AMQP, Integration, Kafka) rather than the Spring Framework core, as evidenced by references to modules, streams, DLQs, and Spring Boot 1.x.

U1 (alternative DLQ) is implemented as a configurable policy on the existing bus message-broker producer, leveraging a DeadLetterPublishingMessageHandler-style hook that adds the original exception + stack-trace header, rather than building a new DLQ subsystem.

U2 (CDC source module) is implemented as a new XD source module wrapping an existing CDC library (Debezium-style) for the binlog/wal tailing, with adapter sinks to the existing broker, Hadoop, and JDBC sink modules, instead of writing a database log parser from scratch.

U3 (Rabbit cluster HA/FT) is implemented natively in spring-amqp using a clustered ConnectionFactory with automatic connection/topology recovery and node-list based addressing, rather than a sidecar proxy.
U4 (Gemfire 8.1 + Spring Data Gosling) is treated as a synchronization/dependency upgrade with API compatibility shims, not a feature add.

U5 (colocated deployment + leader election) is implemented using the existing SPI's leader-election hooks (e.g., over ZooKeeper) and a 'co-located' container profile that shares a single JVM for all modules of a stream.
U6 and U7 are dependency upgrades whose primary risk is JMX and Kafka client API breakage; no new features are introduced.
U8 is a pure BOM/POM synchronization against Spring Boot 1.2.3 plus a propagated transitive dependency list; no semantic changes are introduced beyond what upstream provides.

All work is performed in Java 8 (consistent with Spring Boot 1.2.3 era); unit tests use JUnit/Mockito and integration tests use the existing test harnesses (Spring AMQP test, embedded Kafka, embedded ZooKeeper, embedded GemFire, H2).
Backwards compatibility is preserved for all public SPI and configuration surface; deprecations are introduced where required.
assumptions: A single senior developer performs all activities (no team parallelism, no hand-off overhead).
An 8-hour productive workday is used; meetings, builds, and CI waits are not modeled separately but are absorbed in the per-activity estimates.
All required external infrastructure for testing (Rabbit cluster nodes, ZooKeeper ensemble, GemFire locator, Kafka brokers, MySQL with binlog, Hadoop target) is available or easily provisioned in CI.

Upstream dependencies (Spring Boot 1.2.3, Spring Data Gosling GA, GemFire 8.1, SI milestone/GA, SI Kafka, RabbitMQ) are already released or release-aligned to the planned work window, so the team is not blocked by external release dates.
Existing XD source/sink module SDKs (Module, MessageBus, Container SPI) are stable and require no refactoring for U1, U2, or U5.
The CDC source module is built against MySQL binlog only in this increment; Oracle/Postgres SQL Server adapters are out of scope and left for follow-up work.
The leader-election mechanism for U5 is assumed to use ZooKeeper (already a transitive dependency of XD); a custom Raft implementation is out of scope.
Documentation effort covers user-facing reference docs and release notes only; no marketing or migration guides beyond the release notes are included.
Code review, refactoring, and final polish are budgeted as a single end-of-increment activity rather than per-feature; defect fixes from upgrades are merged into the corresponding upgrade activity.

activities.activity_description: Branch setup, build/CI baseline, dependency repo configuration, integration test environment provisioning (Rabbit cluster, ZooKeeper, Kafka, GemFire, MySQL with binlog), and a planning pass over the 8 user stories.

activities.activity_name: U1: Alternative DLQ configuration - design and implementation
activities.activity_description: Add a configuration property/builder option to specify an alternative DLQ target. Extend the message-broker producer to publish to the configured DLQ on error, attaching headers for the original exception class, message, and full stack trace.

activities.activity_name: U1: DLQ unit/integration tests and documentation
activities.activity_description: Unit tests for the new configuration, integration tests verifying header presence on failed messages, and short reference-doc updates.

activities.activity_name: U2: CDC source module - architecture and design
activities.activity_description: Define the source module's options (server id, table include/exclude, snapshot mode, server name), module contract, lifecycle, and how it integrates with the XD message bus. Decide on the underlying CDC library and snapshot strategy.
Implement the module: bootstrap, snapshot phase, streaming phase, schema change events, restart/resume from checkpoint, and translation to XD messages.

activities.activity_name: U2: Sink integrations for CDC events
activities.activity_description: Wire the CDC source to broker (Kafka/Rabbit), Hadoop (HDFS), and DB sinks. Provide small adapters/mappers to ensure consistent event payload structure across sinks.
Unit tests for the source module logic, integration tests against an embedded MySQL with binlog enabled, and end-to-end tests verifying delivery to each sink target.
User-facing reference for the CDC source module, including options, snapshot behavior, and recovery semantics.

activities.activity_name: U3: Spring AMQP Rabbit cluster connection - design
activities.activity_description: Define the cluster connection configuration model (node addresses, virtual host, credentials, topology-recovery policy, address-shuffle behavior) and the impact on connection caching.

activities.activity_name: U3: Spring AMQP Rabbit cluster - implementation
activities.activity_description: Implement a CachingConnectionFactory-based cluster connector with node-list addressing, automatic topology recovery, and reconnection/backoff. Expose relevant properties on RabbitAdmin and listener containers.
Integration tests covering node shutdown, network partition simulation, and verification that producers/consumers fail over without message loss and that declared topology is re-applied on recovery.

activities.activity_name: U4: Gemfire 8.1 / Spring Data Gosling synchronization
activities.activity_description: Bump Gemfire to 8.1 and Spring Data Gemfire to Gosling GA, resolve transitive dependency alignment, and apply minor API compatibility shims (renamed classes, deprecated methods).
Re-run the XD Gemfire sink and any related test suites against the upgraded version; address any test failures.
Design the colocation container profile, module wiring within a single JVM, and the integration points with the existing leader-election SPI for failover between containers.

activities.activity_name: U5: Leader election and failover implementation
activities.activity_description: Implement per-stream leader election over ZooKeeper so that when the leader container fails, a follower container takes over the stream's modules; ensure message offsets/state are consistent on takeover.

activities.activity_name: U5: Colocated deployment and failover testing
activities.activity_description: Integration tests for single-container colocation, leader crash recovery, split-brain avoidance, and state/offset preservation across failover.

activities.activity_name: U6: Spring Integration upgrade to milestone/GA
activities.activity_description: Bump Spring Integration dependency to the target milestone/GA, particularly for JMX improvements; resolve any compilation breakage.
Re-run the full test suite; specifically verify JMX-exposed MBeans, notifications, and any module that depends on the channel/adapter behavior changes.
Bump Spring Integration Kafka to the target release; align Kafka client version as required by the upgrade; resolve any API breakage.
Re-run Kafka-based source/sink tests; verify partition assignment, offset commit, and error-handling semantics with the upgraded client.
Update parent/inherited BOM to Spring Boot 1.2.3; resolve conflicts with the project's own dependency management section.

Update logback, jackson, gemfire, h2, javax-mail, undertow, joda-time, nekohtml, activemq, antlr2, commons-dbcp2, tomcat, aspectj, groovy, crashub, jetty, elasticsearch, flyway, freemarker, jdom2, liquibase, mockito, mongodb, slf4j, spring-cloud-connectors, spring-security, jedis, spring-ws versions to those mandated by Spring Boot 1.2.3.

activities.activity_name: U8: Test suite fixes from dependency upgrades
activities.activity_description: Fix tests broken by API or behavior changes in upgraded dependencies (e.g., Mockito API changes, Jackson 2.5 changes, Spring Security 4.0 changes).
Update build plugins, CI configuration, and any profile that depends on the upgraded versions; ensure the full multi-module build runs green.
Run the full end-to-end test matrix combining the new features (CDC, colocated streams, Rabbit cluster, DLQ headers) to catch interaction regressions.
